headline: Florida Becomes First State to Sue OpenAI and Sam Altman Over ChatGPT Safety Failures
raw_snippet: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a first-of-its-kind state lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman personally, alleging ChatGPT aided mass shooters (including the FSU and USF incidents), encouraged suicides, and addicted minors. The 83-page complaint includes 10 counts spanning deceptive trade practices, negligence, product liability, fraudulent misrepresentation, and public nuisance. Florida seeks to hold Altman personally liable — the first time a state or federal government has attempted to impose personal CEO liability for AI-related harms.

headline: Trump Signs Executive Order Seeking Voluntary 30-Day Pre-Release Access to Frontier AI Models
raw_snippet: President Trump signed an executive order on June 2 asking AI companies to voluntarily provide the government access to frontier models up to 30 days before public release for cybersecurity testing. The order explicitly bars mandatory licensing or preclearance. An earlier draft had proposed a 90-day review window. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the order, calling it the right balance between safety and innovation.

headline: Sam Altman Meets Bipartisan Congressional Leaders and White House Officials on AI Policy
raw_snippet: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met with White House officials, House Speaker Mike Johnson, and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries in Washington on June 3, discussing the new AI executive order and broader AI policy. Altman wrote on X that the executive order 'gets the balance right' between developing the best models and ensuring safety.

headline: OpenAI and Oracle Break Ground on $16 Billion Stargate Data Center Campus in Michigan
raw_snippet: OpenAI, Oracle, Related Digital, Blackstone, and Walbridge held a groundbreaking ceremony for 'The Barn,' a $16 billion Stargate data center campus in Saline Township, Michigan, with Governor Whitmer in attendance. The campus will comprise three single-story data center buildings with over 1 GW of capacity, creating 2,500+ union construction jobs. It is the single largest economic investment in Michigan history. OpenAI committed $10M to expand the Saline Recreation Center and $14M to fire services and farmland preservation.

headline: Microsoft Unveils Seven In-House MAI Models at Build 2026, Signaling Reduced OpenAI Dependence
raw_snippet: Microsoft announced seven new AI models under the MAI family at Build 2026, led by MAI-Thinking-1 (35B parameters, 256K context window). After tuning for McKinsey, Microsoft claims MAI outperformed GPT-5.5 on quality with 10x better cost efficiency and matched Claude Opus 4.6 on coding benchmarks. The move marks Microsoft's deliberate pivot toward 'long-term self-sufficiency' from OpenAI, following their revised partnership that ended OpenAI's IP exclusivity.

headline: Anthropic Confidentially Files S-1 for IPO at $965 Billion Valuation, Beating OpenAI to Market
raw_snippet: Anthropic confidentially filed its S-1 with the SEC on June 1, moving ahead of OpenAI in the race to go public. Anthropic's post-money valuation of $965 billion tops OpenAI's $852 billion. With Anthropic's revenue run rate at $47 billion (up from $10B last year), analysts say whichever company reaches markets first will have an advantage in the AI IPO race. OpenAI filed its own confidential S-1 on May 22, targeting a fall listing.

headline: OpenAI Targets September IPO at Up to $1 Trillion Valuation After Confidential S-1 Filing
raw_snippet: OpenAI is targeting a public listing as early as September 2026 at a valuation above $1 trillion, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan leading the deal. The company filed its confidential S-1 with the SEC on May 22. Revenue hit $2B per month but OpenAI loses $1.22 for every $1 earned. The filing comes days after Anthropic filed at $965 billion, setting up simultaneous IPO competition.

headline: OpenAI Expands Codex Beyond Developers With Sites, Annotations, and Six Role-Specific Enterprise Plugins
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced the largest Codex expansion since its enterprise launch on June 3, introducing Sites (hosted interactive web apps), Annotations (in-place editing), and six role-specific plugins aggregating 62 business applications including Snowflake, Figma, and Salesforce with 110 automated skills. Codex now has 5 million weekly active users (6x since February), with knowledge workers at 20% of users and growing 3x faster than developers. Dedicated plugins target data analytics, creative production, sales, product design, equity investing, and investment banking.

headline: OpenAI Updates GPT-Rosalind With GPT-5.5 for Life Sciences, Expands Global Research Access
raw_snippet: OpenAI released an updated GPT-Rosalind series on June 3, combining GPT-5.5's agentic coding and tool-use capabilities with stronger model intelligence in medicinal chemistry and genomics. The model completes long-horizon quantitative biology analyses using 31% fewer tokens than GPT-5.5. For the first time, the research preview was opened to eligible organizations worldwide (previously restricted), requiring legitimate scientific research with clear public benefit and enterprise-grade security.

headline: OpenAI Rolls Out ChatGPT Dreaming V3 Memory Architecture Upgrade for Plus and Pro Users
raw_snippet: OpenAI began rolling out Dreaming V3 on June 4, a background process that synthesizes memory automatically and replaces the saved-memories list as ChatGPT's core memory system. The upgrade enables time-aware memory updates (e.g., converting future plans to past events), raises factual recall from 41.5% to 82.8% on internal evals, and delivers a 5x reduction in compute cost, making Free-tier rollout practical. Plus and Pro users also get doubled memory capacity.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Lockdown Mode to Combat Prompt Injection Data Exfiltration
raw_snippet: OpenAI began rolling out Lockdown Mode on June 4 for personal ChatGPT accounts and self-serve Business accounts. When enabled, it disables web access, image responses, Deep Research, Agent Mode, Canvas networking, live connectors, and file downloads — reducing prompt-injection attack surfaces. A separate 'Active Sessions' feature now lets users review all signed-in devices and end unrecognized sessions, showing device type, location, and sign-in time.

headline: OpenAI Launches Conversion-Optimized Ad Campaigns in ChatGPT, Shifting Toward Performance Channel
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched conversion-optimized ad campaigns in ChatGPT on June 5, moving beyond reach-and-traffic into direct performance advertising. Advertisers who configured the OpenAI Pixel or Conversions API by June 1 gained early access. The shift follows the move from $60 CPM to $3-$5 CPC pricing after CPMs eroded within ten weeks of launch. OpenAI projects $2.5B in ad revenue for 2026, targeting $100B by 2030. Only 20M of 800M weekly users pay for premium tiers (under 3% conversion).

headline: ChatGPT Ads Go Live in the UK, OpenAI's First European Market, With Broader International Expansion Planned
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on June 6 that ChatGPT advertising is now live in the UK — the first European market to receive ads. VP of Monetization Benji Shomair and Global Head of Ads David Dugan confirmed Zalando as a launch partner. Expansion to Japan, South Korea, Brazil, and Mexico is planned in coming weeks. Ads appear only for Free and Go tier users; Plus, Pro, and Enterprise remain ad-free. Only US-based advertisers can buy via the self-serve Ads Manager for now.

headline: OpenAI Plans Largest ChatGPT Overhaul Into 'Superapp' Ahead of IPO, Codenamed Aria
raw_snippet: OpenAI is preparing the largest ChatGPT overhaul since launch, internally codenamed 'Aria,' transforming the chatbot into a 'superapp' combining coding tools, image generation, AI agents, and third-party integrations. Launch partners include Canva, Booking.com, Expedia, Figma, Spotify, Coursera, and Zillow. A senior employee said 'Chat is dead.' The redesign targets the company's 900M weekly users and aims to drive higher-margin business revenue (currently 40%, targeting 50% by year-end) ahead of the planned IPO.

headline: Canada Privacy Commissioners Rule OpenAI Violated Five Privacy Statutes Training ChatGPT on Scraped Data
raw_snippet: Canada's federal and provincial privacy commissioners concluded that OpenAI violated five separate privacy statutes when scraping the public web to train ChatGPT, including health information, political views, and children's data without consent. While the regulators accepted that building LLMs is an 'appropriate purpose,' they found deficiencies across consent, transparency, accuracy, retention, access rights, and accountability. OpenAI committed to corrective measures on a staggered timeline. The finding was released May 6 but continued to drive policy discussion in early June.

headline: OpenAI Published Frontier Governance Framework Mapping Safety Practices to EU AI Act and California Law
raw_snippet: OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework on May 28, mapping internal safety practices to the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for GPAI and California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act (SB 53). The framework covers risk assessment for cyber offense, CBRN risks, harmful manipulation, and loss of control. EU compliance responsibility rests with OpenAI Ireland Limited. EU AI Act transparency rules become fully enforceable August 2, 2026. The framework sets a precedent other frontier labs are expected to match.

headline: ChatGPT Enterprise and EDU Add Workspace Agents With Admin Controls, Free Trial Extended to July 6
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched workspace agents for ChatGPT Enterprise and EDU, replacing custom GPTs with persistent Codex-powered assistants that connect to Slack, Salesforce, and other external apps. Agents can complete multi-step workflows autonomously in the cloud. Admins get role-based controls and activity visibility. The free trial period was extended to July 6, 2026, after which credit-based pricing begins. Default plugin sharing in Codex was also added for eligible workspaces.

headline: EU Preparing to Designate ChatGPT as Very Large Online Search Engine Under Digital Services Act
raw_snippet: The European Commission is preparing to designate ChatGPT as a 'very large online search engine' under the Digital Services Act (DSA), according to sources within the Commission. ChatGPT reported 159.1 million average monthly active recipients in the EU for the six months ending March 31, 2026 — more than triple the 45 million threshold. Designation would trigger stricter obligations around contact channels, criminal activity reporting, transparency on advertising and algorithms, and content moderation within four months.

headline: Altman Discusses $46 Billion Stargate Michigan Investment in CNBC Interview, Addresses IPO Plans
raw_snippet: In a CNBC exclusive interview on June 1, Sam Altman discussed the Stargate data center project in Saline, Michigan, involving $16 billion for site development and an additional $30 billion for infrastructure — totaling $46 billion. At the June 2 'Intelligence at Work' enterprise livestream, Altman disclosed OpenAI's top internal token user consumes approximately 100 billion tokens monthly, and that cost is now the second most common enterprise customer complaint.

headline: U.S. News Asks Whether Other States Will Follow Florida's OpenAI Lawsuit
raw_snippet: Following Florida's first-in-the-nation lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman, U.S. News analyzed whether other state attorneys general will pursue similar actions. The Florida case establishes a potential template for personal CEO liability in AI harms cases. With over 20 existing lawsuits against OpenAI from families of shooting victims, suicide victims, and minors, the Florida AG's action may catalyze a wave of state-level AI enforcement.
